study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Zhang et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Parsing the heterogeneity of brain-symptom associations in autism spectrum disorder via random forest with homogeneous canonical correlation

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used both ABIDE I and ABIDE II datasets. 1094 participants from ABIDE I and 1100 participants from ABIDE II passed preprocessing. After exclusions (32 for failed segmentation, 31 for outlier TIV, 2 for age inconsistency), the final sample comprised 1146 typically developing controls (TDC) and 571 ASD cases.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The study analyzed both structural neuroimaging data and phenotypic data provided by the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) (Di Martino et al., 2017; Di Martino et al., 2014)." ... "We had 1094 participants in ABIDE I and 1100 participants in ABIDE II who passed the preprocessing"

answer.ABIDE (I+II): normative model training (TDC, N=1146) and clinical application (ASD cases, N=571 for subtyping and case-control classification)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: TDC (N=1146) from ABIDE I+II were used to fit a multivariate linear regression normative model of gray matter volume (GMV) by age, gender, and TIV. ASD cases (N=571) were then evaluated against this normative model to estimate volumetric deviations, which were used for brain-symptom association-based subtyping (RFHCC algorithm) and case-control classification.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we fitted a multivariate linear regression model for the regional GMV by age, gender and TIV using the controls." ... "The model was then applied to the corresponding brain regions of the cases, and the model residuals were used to estimate volumetric deviations for each case from the typical developing trajectory."

model-1.model-name: multivariate linear regression normative model of GMV

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using all 1146 TDC. The paper does not describe a separate train/test split for the normative model itself; all 1146 controls were used to fit the regression model (GMV ~ gender + TIV + age + age^2). The model was then applied to the 571 ASD cases to compute deviations.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "we fitted a multivariate linear regression model for the regional GMV by age, gender and TIV using the controls." ... "Finally, the data from 1146 controls and 571 cases entered the following analyses."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age information is reported for the TDC group (N=1146) in Table 1. Since all 1146 TDC were used for the normative model without a separate train/test split, the overall-phase and train-phase values are the same. Age unit is years.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex information is reported for the TDC group in Table 1 as Gender(M/F) = 868/278, totaling 1146. Since all 1146 TDC were used for the normative model without a separate train/test split, the overall-phase and train-phase values are the same. Female percentage: 278/1146 = 24.3%; Male percentage: 868/1146 = 75.7%.
